title: Esther 1
paragraphs: ¹ In the days of Ahasuerus — the Ahasuerus who ruled over a hundred and twenty-seven provinces stretching from India to Ethiopia — ² when he was sitting on his royal throne in Shushan the palace, ³ in the third year of his reign, he gave a banquet for all his officials and servants. The military commanders of Persia and Media, the nobles, and the governors of the provinces were all in attendance. ⁴ For a full hundred and eighty days he put on a display of his kingdom's glorious wealth and his own magnificent splendor. ⁵ When those days were over, the king held another feast for all the people present in Shushan the palace, great and small alike — a seven-day celebration in the courtyard of the palace garden.

⁶ The courtyard was hung with white and blue linen curtains, fastened by cords of fine linen and purple thread to silver rings on marble pillars. The couches were of gold and silver, set on a mosaic floor of red and blue and white and black marble. ⁷ Wine was served in golden cups, each one different from the next, and the royal wine flowed freely — as befitted the king's generosity. ⁸ The drinking was without restriction; the king had instructed every palace steward to let each guest do as he wished. ⁹ Meanwhile, Queen Vashti gave her own banquet for the women inside the royal palace. ¹⁰ On the seventh day, when the king's heart was merry with wine, he commanded his seven eunuchs — Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas — who attended him personally,

¹¹ to bring Queen Vashti before him wearing her royal crown, so that the people and officials could admire her beauty, for she was lovely to look at. ¹² But Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command, delivered through his eunuchs. The king was furious, and his anger blazed within him. ¹³ He consulted the wise men who understood the law — for it was his custom to seek the opinion of those versed in law and justice. ¹⁴ His closest advisors were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media who had direct access to the king and held the highest positions in the kingdom. ¹⁵ He asked them, "What does the law say we should do to Queen Vashti, since she has not obeyed the command of King Ahasuerus delivered through his eunuchs?"

¹⁶ Memucan answered before the king and the princes, "Queen Vashti has wronged not only the king but also every official and every people in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus. ¹⁷ The story of what the queen has done will spread to all the women and encourage them to despise their husbands. They will say, 'King Ahasuerus commanded Queen Vashti to be brought before him, and she refused!' ¹⁸ And this very day the noblewomen of Persia and Media who hear what the queen has done will repeat it to all the king's officials, and there will be no end of disrespect and resentment. ¹⁹ If it pleases the king, let a royal decree go out from him — and let it be recorded in the laws of the Persians and Medes so that it cannot be repealed — that Vashti is never again to appear before King Ahasuerus, and that the king should give her royal position to someone more worthy. ²⁰ When the king's decree is proclaimed throughout his vast empire, every wife will honor her husband, from the greatest to the least."

²¹ This advice pleased the king and his officials, and the king acted on Memucan's proposal. ²² He sent letters to all his royal provinces, to each province in its own script and to each people in their own language, declaring that every man should be master in his own home, and that this should be announced in each people's tongue.
